propositions: prev_snapshot.json currently stores full ACLI payload (27.1 MB at HEAD) but only needs to store a bare key-set dictionary {jira_key: {}} (19,960 bytes), reducing storage from 228.1 MB / 4.5 MB per day to a negligible amount.

Over 400 real revisions, 218 consecutive prev snapshot pairs have identical key sets, meaning they produce no commits; when key sets differ the mean symmetric difference is only 1.78 keys, validating that the key-set optimization captures the essential state.

Corpus mutation-diff testing over four real snapshot pairs with full prev versus key-set prev showed zero difference in observable mutations reaching Jira, and the production call-site filter already strips local-state emissions, making the change safe.

With a full prev snapshot, shrinking fetch windows or project re-targeting cause compute_mutations to emit 973-998 unbound_local create mutations that are filtered by the call-site; a key-set prev eliminates these at the source without changing Jira-facing behavior.

The key-set shape must be a dict not a set because prev-shape-sensitive consumers (check_dual_identity_complete and differ's local-only/emit-both arms) use local_state[key] or {} guards requiring mapping entries.
